title: Conjecture 1 (Cereceda)
statement_text: If $G$ is a $k$-degenerate graph on $n$ vertices, then $R_{k+2}(G)$ has diameter $O(n^2)$.
context_text: Cereceda conjectured this quadratic diameter bound for the reconfiguration graph with $k+2$ colors on $k$-degenerate graphs, and the bound would be best possible. Despite several efforts and partial results, the conjecture remains open even for $k=2$.
paper_contribution: The paper does not directly prove any case of this conjecture; it is cited as foundational motivation for the study of reconfiguration of colorings of planar graphs, and the techniques developed (reducible configurations, valid recoloring sequences) are in the same research program.
paper_title: An update on reconfiguring $10$-colorings of planar graphs

title: Problem 3
statement_text: What is the minimum integer $\kappa$ such that for every planar graph $G$ with $n$ vertices, $R_{\kappa}(G)$ has diameter $O(n)$?
context_text: The reconfiguration graph $R_k(G)$ has as vertices all proper $k$-colorings of $G$, two colorings being adjacent if they differ in the color of exactly one vertex; so the distance between two colorings is the minimum number of single-vertex recolorings, keeping the coloring proper, needed to transform one into the other. Cereceda conjectured that $R_{k+2}(G)$ has diameter $O(n^2)$ for $k$-degenerate $n$-vertex graphs. Planar graphs are $5$-degenerate and have maximum average degree less than $6$, so known results (Feghali; Bousquet and Perarnau, who show that $R_c(G)$ has diameter at most $(k+1)n$ for $k$-degenerate $G$ and $c\ge2k+2$) give that $R_8(G)$ has diameter $O(n(\log n)^7)$ and $R_{12}(G)$ has diameter at most $6n$ for planar $G$. The authors prove that $R_{10}(G)$ has diameter at most $8n$ for every $n$-vertex planar graph, so $\kappa\le10$. Conversely, the $6$-coloring of the icosahedron giving opposite vertices the same color is an isolated vertex of $R_6$, so $\kappa\ge7$. A natural candidate planar graph with quadratic diameter of $R_7$, built from copies of a cylinder obtained by cutting the toroidal drawing of $K_7$, is $3$-degenerate and chordal and hence has linear diameter by a result of Bartier and Bousquet; so the authors cannot exclude $\kappa=7$.
paper_title: An update on reconfiguring $10$-colorings of planar graphs
